title: Anatomy of an Effective Pull Request
learning_objectives: Explain the difference between what a PR is and what makes one effective
Identify the essential sections of a well-structured PR description
Understand the reviewer's perspective: what they need to evaluate a PR
Distinguish between the commit body (the why) and the PR description (the what and how to review)
outline: What is a PR in context: a request for a human code review, not just a merge
The reviewer's perspective: what do they need to say yes?
Essential PR sections: Overview, What Changed, How to Test, Screenshots/Evidence
Optional sections: Related Issues, Breaking Changes, Deployment Notes
Writing the 'Why': motivation belongs in the PR description as well as commit bodies
Real-world examples: annotated PRs from well-maintained open-source projects

helm_context.feature: PR quality for all Helm feature development
helm_context.deliverable: Understanding of PR anatomy, applied in L06-L07

criteria: Can name the essential sections of a PR description from memory
Can articulate what a reviewer needs to efficiently evaluate a PR
Can explain the difference between commit body and PR description purpose

professor_constraints: Keep this conceptual — no hands-on exercise, just understanding
Use 2-3 annotated real PR examples from open-source projects
Helm-specific examples: what would a PR description look like for adding the drag-to-time-block feature?
Set up the 'why' for L06: this lesson is the blueprint, L06 is building the template
